summary: Crunchy, golden, lightly sweet fried dough nuggets scented with nutmeg, made to snack on by the handful.
story: Chin chin is a crunchy fried pastry that is a staple of Nigerian parties, Christmas tables and school bags. It is made in big batches, stored in airtight tins and shared around.

steps.title: Rub in the butter
steps.text: Combine the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt and nutmeg in a large bowl. Rub in the cold butter with your fingertips until the mixture looks like coarse breadcrumbs with no big lumps.

steps.title: Form a stiff dough
steps.text: Beat the egg with 1/4 cup of the milk and mix it in. Add more milk a spoonful at a time until the dough just holds together. It should be firm and not sticky, stiffer than bread dough.

steps.title: Knead and rest
steps.text: Knead on a lightly floured surface for 2 to 3 minutes until smooth. Cover and rest for 15 minutes so the gluten relaxes and rolling is easier.

steps.title: Roll thin
steps.text: Roll the dough to about 4 mm, no thicker, since thin pieces fry crisp all the way through. Use a knife or pastry wheel to cut into small squares or diamonds about 1.5 cm across.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Heat the oil to about 170°C in a deep pot. A test piece should sink then rise within 3 to 4 seconds, surrounded by gentle bubbles.

steps.title: Fry in batches
steps.text: Fry a handful at a time, stirring constantly with a slotted spoon so the pieces colour evenly. They are done after 3 to 5 minutes, when light golden brown. They darken a little after leaving the oil, so lift them slightly early.

steps.title: Drain and cool
steps.text: Drain on paper towels, then spread out in a single layer to cool fully. They crisp up as they cool. Store in an airtight container once cold.

tips: If chin chin comes out hard rather than crunchy, the dough was too stiff or rolled too thick.
Fry in small batches. Overcrowding drops the oil temperature and makes the pieces oily.
Stored airtight, chin chin keeps for 2 to 3 weeks.
Do not store until completely cold or steam will soften them.

swaps.swap: Use margarine or 3 tbsp neutral oil. Texture is nearly the same, with a little less richness.
For a vegan version, use plant milk and omit the egg, adding a little extra milk. The dough is slightly crisper and paler.
